meta.title: About me | Sefinek
meta.description: Meet Sefinek - a self-taught developer from Poland interested in network security, open source, home servers and building things that actually work.

label: Get to know me
heading: About me
intro: Hi, I'm Sefinek - self-taught, from Poland, with an obsession with privacy, network security and creating things that do some good. I like being in control of what I run - preferably on my own hardware, humming somewhere in the corner of my room.

bio.title: Who I am
bio.beginning: My computing journey started when I was about 13. At first, I tried making websites with various online builders, but their limitations soon started getting in the way. The results often felt basic, so I decided to try building something myself. I found an HTML course on YouTube, and that's where it all really began.
bio.programming: Later, I became interested in batch files and eventually in programming in C# and C++. At first, it was mostly curiosity and a desire to experiment. I didn't have a specific plan or a bigger goal. I simply enjoyed figuring out how things worked, changing things and finding my own solutions.
bio.servers: My first major step towards servers came when I needed somewhere to run my own Discord bot. That's when I bought my first VPS, probably running Ubuntu 18.04.
bio.today: Today, I mainly see programming as a tool for bringing my own ideas to life. I'm much more interested in servers, service management and extensive infrastructure. I'm also paying more attention to radio infrastructure, which gives me a whole new area to experiment with.
bio.learning: I learned most things on my own. Even as a kid, I rarely asked anyone for help - this was before AI tools became widely available, so I had to find answers myself, mainly in documentation, on forums and through trial and error. Over time, things I originally built just for myself began to be used by others too.

firstSteps.title: First steps
firstSteps.description: Even as a kid, I was quite different from my peers. They preferred spending time gaming, while I preferred doing something useful - even on hardware where Tibia could lag, let alone playing YouTube videos. Still, I appreciated what I had. It was some Acer with Windows 7 and 2GB of RAM - that's where I took my first steps with HTML. Before that, my first computer ran Windows XP and had a hard drive of about 50GB.

work.title: What I do
work.infrastructure: I spend most of my time on server administration, network infrastructure and related topics. At home, I maintain my own environment, mainly based on Proxmox, with numerous machines and services, including honeypots. I also maintain blocklists and analyze malicious IP addresses using OSINT. The collected data then goes to SniffCat and AbuseIPDB.
work.openSource: I publish most of my projects as open source. I like an open and reasonably permissive approach to software and sharing code. I mainly use programming to automate tasks, integrate services and build my own solutions and new platforms.
work.radio: I'm currently also focusing on MeshCore and radio infrastructure - repeaters, LoRa, off-grid power, antennas and SDR. When needed, I do some soldering too.

personal.title: Beyond technology
personal.music: I almost always listen to music while working.
personal.photography: I sometimes do photography, currently mostly with a drone.
personal.anime: I used to watch anime occasionally, but these days it barely interests me at all.
personal.games: Games have also taken a back seat - I'd much rather do something useful.
